body:
## Problem and evidence

Found while continuing the owner's M7 request: “Is work happening in the background now? If not, can we continue our work on M7?”

The actual-main/systemd fixture for #583 reached readiness, queued one signed synthetic award, passed graceful/manual/automatic restart preservation, then observed online_state=true with the award still queued and no background flush. Original attempt04 remains FAIL; no thread or cleanup errors. The local peer opened while ConnectivityMonitor's initial forced probe could still be running. This startup transition is now causally reproduced and repaired: the baseline leaves the signed award queued across two online monitor probes15s apart, while the seven-line startup-observation handoff flushes it exactly once. Focused actual-main/systemd and ten component cases pass; installed-image acceptance remains open.

Current prepared fork source calls a startup reachability probe and conditionally flushes, then starts ConnectivityMonitor. That worker performs a separate initial probe and only flushes on later false→true transitions. A connection returning between the two initial observations could therefore remain online without flushing the pending queue. Current upstream2d19684e0800f6da33ff1841d27e083c1e467142 has the same sequence. Narrow upstream open-issue search for pending awards returned no result; not an exhaustive absence claim.

Evidence in coordinator: docs/qa-logs/2026-10-14-proxy-service-runtime/attempt04 and startup-window-upstream.json. Normal offline→online qualification now explicitly observes the initial false result; its success must not close this separate startup case.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] A bounded no-NIC VM fixture controls connectivity across the startup probe and first worker probe; original probe/queue/peer traces show whether the suspected missed transition occurs.
- [x] If reproduced, exact-source correction delivers the queued signed award once when connectivity returns in that window, with original native/service result0 and SQLite integrity/queue receipts. Otherwise record why the hypothesis was disproved.
- [x] Already-online, persistent-offline, ordinary reconnect, authentication refusal and stop/restart preserve expected queue/account behavior; no timer bypass or real account/provider required.
- [ ] Installed composed-source service proof covers the accepted repair before the next candidate is designated; upstream contribution disposition is recorded under #585 after initial build.

Can this be done on the VM? Yes. All timing/queue/service facts are synthetic no-network VM behavior; no physical device action is needed. Existing service bounds and original-result/cleanup ownership apply.

Already written: shipped behavior may retain awards in the pending queue across startup. No queue deletion or owner data repair is authorized by this issue. Qualification must prove existing pending rows survive and flush without duplicate application.

## Current integration and next evidence

The repair is published in next at e483a7f0925e7ebb56335133a5de423269390945 as raofflineproxy patch021. Exact prepared Python/native inputs and original baseline/candidate/service/component receipts are retained under docs/qa-logs/2026-10-14-proxy-startup-runtime and the related source/service packets. The next engineering GENERIC_X64 image includes it. Verify its actual installed service and native library on default boot before closing the last criterion or designating a candidate. Current source qualification is recorded in [the detailed result](https://github.com/pixelelated/distribution/issues/588#issuecomment-6175550586); no real account, device, or cloud mutation was used.
